What happens to my Proton Mail when I die?

By the Afterkeep research team · Reviewed on 16 Nov 2026

Short answer: Proton's built-in route is Emergency Access, which you set up in advance. On any paid Proton plan you can choose up to five emergency contacts, each with a Proton Mail address, who can request access to your account if you die or are incapacitated. Access is granted automatically after the waiting period you choose (1 to 30 days) unless you deny it. Proton's help pages describe no other way for family to get in. Free accounts inactive for more than 24 months could be deleted, along with emails, files and passwords.

Key facts

  • Emergency Access: up to 5 contacts, on all paid plans
  • You and your contact both need a Proton Mail address
  • Wait time 1 to 30 days; Proton notifies you so you can deny it
  • Free accounts inactive over 24 months could be deleted

How do I prepare my Proton Mail account?

  1. Check your plan: Proton says Emergency Access is available on all paid Proton plans, and both you and your contact must have a Proton Mail address.
  2. Add a contact: sign in at mail.proton.me, open Settings, select Recovery, scroll to Emergency access and click Add emergency contact. Enter their Proton Mail address, choose a wait time (30, 14, 7, 3, 2 or 1 day) and confirm with your password. You can add up to five.
  3. Create a recovery phrase too (Settings, Recovery, Recovery phrase, Create recovery phrase) and keep the PDF outside Proton, for example printed and stored with your important documents. Proton says not to keep it in Proton Drive or Proton Pass, because you couldn't reach them if locked out.
  4. Record in your digital estate plan your Proton address, your plan, and who your emergency contacts are.
  5. After a death: the emergency contact signs into their own Proton account, opens Settings, Recovery, Emergency access, finds the person under 'People who trust me' and clicks Request access.
  6. Once the wait time ends, they click Access account, enter their own password and choose Switch account.

Read the official policy ↗

What documents do heirs need?

  • Your own Proton Mail account, with you added as their emergency contact
  • Your own Proton password, to switch into their account once access is granted

How long does it take?

Access is granted automatically at the end of the waiting period the account owner chose (30, 14, 7, 3, 2 or 1 day), or sooner if they approve it. For free accounts, Proton says accounts inactive for more than 24 months could be deleted and it sends reminder emails 30, 15 and 7 days before the scheduled deletion. Proton says it never deletes paid accounts for inactivity.

What can't be recovered?

  • Everything in a deleted account: Proton says deletion permanently removes emails, contacts, calendars, passwords and files
  • The email address itself: Proton says deleted addresses generally can't be recovered

Frequently asked questions

What happens to my Proton Mail when I die?

Proton's built-in route is Emergency Access, which you set up in advance. On any paid Proton plan you can choose up to five emergency contacts, each with a Proton Mail address, who can request access to your account if you die or are incapacitated. Access is granted automatically after the waiting period you choose (1 to 30 days) unless you deny it. Proton's help pages describe no other way for family to get in. Free accounts inactive for more than 24 months could be deleted, along with emails, files and passwords.

What happens to my Proton Mail account when I die?

Unless you set up Emergency Access, Proton's help pages describe no way for family to get in. With it, a contact you chose can request access and gets it automatically after the waiting period you set. Free accounts inactive for more than 24 months could be deleted.

Is Proton Emergency Access free?

No. Proton says it's available on all paid Proton plans. You and your emergency contact must both have a Proton Mail address.

Can my emergency contact use a Gmail or Outlook address?

No. Proton says the emergency contact must have a Proton Mail email address.

Will Proton delete a free account after the owner dies?

It can. Proton says free accounts inactive for more than 24 months could be deleted, with reminder emails 30, 15 and 7 days before. Its inactive account policy doesn't apply to paid plans.

What is a Proton recovery phrase?

A 12-word, one-time backup password that lets the account holder reset their password and recover encrypted data. Keep it somewhere safe outside Proton. Emergency Access is Proton's feature for giving someone else access.
